fatal_errors: The proposed coated-particle intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor into aligned, bicontinuous RHEA and Cu networks.
None of the cited evidence demonstrates that a W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf interlayer at a W/Cu interface lowers thermal boundary resistance or increases the effective thermal conductivity of a W-Cu composite.

The claimed retention of mechanical durability and neutron-irradiation resistance is extrapolated from irradiation studies of isolated HEA films and unrelated WC-HEA mechanical data, rather than tests of the proposed W-Cu composite.
The asserted 10–20% conductivity increase has no cited quantitative basis.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad engineering objective and supplies a directly comparable uncoated W-Cu control plus a reasonably falsifiable testing plan. However, it is a speculative alternative rather than a reconstruction of the target: it omits selective Ti removal in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h, aligned Cu-channel formation, the continuous RHEA ligament network, and the spontaneously formed W-rich passivating interface. Its cited studies support the general thermal stability and ion-irradiation tolerance of certain refractory HEAs, but not enhanced W/Cu interfacial heat transport, composite-scale mechanical retention, or neutron tolerance. The boundary conditions are also too generic and extend beyond the evidence. Thus, although novel and experimentally testable, the central conductivity and durability claims are insufficiently supported.
